independentSourceFindings.reason: The atom is a defensible bounded operationalization. BW prints vector p = mv and asks for states suitable for momentum balances. SN LK 11 names two-body problems and signs. SL explicitly sums the two mass–velocity products in a straight collision. The native scope has 48 target views and 25 further views in which the goal is reached as a prerequisite. Some target locations need a corrected source attribution or placement.
unsupportedClaims: BY's two-body momentum support is in Ph10, while the native target sits under Ph8.3. MV's cited balance is in the qualification phase, while the native place says introductory year 10. ST's stronger two-body balance evidence is at elevated level on p. 79.

SL's nuclear-physics heading and SN's relativity heading do not identify the mechanics clauses that support this atom. NI's optional route to force through momentum and RP's conditional Sek I treatment do not establish a compulsory two-body atom there.
BE/BB p. 21 belongs to one selectable theme under p. 17. Neither the school-form condition nor the selection rule supports a universal Gymnasium obligation.

independentSourceFindings.reason: BW, HE, BY Ph10 and SL support simple momentum conservation and recoil without requiring the advanced proof. The actual Bayern Grade 8 target placement is not substantiated by the supplied Ph8 pages. The BE/BB introductory elective pages also retain their school-form and selection conditions.
unsupportedClaims: The current Bayern Grade 8 conservation target placement is not substantiated by the supplied Ph8 pages; the supplied explicit momentum-conservation support is at Grade 10.

independentSourceFindings.reason: BW, HE, MV and SL provide direct recoil support. SL p. 12 explicitly connects the vector sum for a mechanically closed system with recoil. MV p. 21 allows simple recoil at GK, and ST p. 79 explicitly relates recoil to momentum conservation at elevated level. A qualitative before-and-after explanation fits these clauses. Their scope is narrower than attribution of the same obligation to every current target place.
unsupportedClaims: The 70 native target views are product placements. BE/BB's school-form-limited elective theme gives recoil as a possible context. NI's supplied pages do not establish the specific recoil outcome as mandatory. ST p. 54 covers momentum as a state quantity at basic level.
BY Ph10 supports conservation and the interaction-law connection, while the displayed goal sits under Ph8.3. The SL recoil clause is in force and motion, while the displayed place is nuclear physics.
A requirement for a general Newtonian derivation or a numerical solution for an astronaut's final speed does not follow from this qualitative recoil atom.

independentSourceFindings.reason: BW p.27 actually prints F=Δp/Δt; p.57 makes listed formulas binding and locates the starred section in Klasse 10. SN LK11 provides the momentum-rate context, with the interval mean a bounded preparatory operationalization. Actual RATE-M targets are BW and SN LK. BE/BB support remains conditional elective content under p.17, and prerequisite-only appearances elsewhere establish no nationwide target obligation.
inspectedOfficialPages: official-pages/01-BW-official-extract.pdf: original physical pp.27, 57; p.27 formula graphics inspected
official-pages/19-SN-official-extract.pdf: original physical p.58; differential-law graphic inspected

independentSourceFindings.reason: The printed BW formula on physical p. 27 is F = Δp/Δt. Page 57 makes the printed formulas binding and places the starred section in Klasse 10. For a varying force, the quotient is correctly interpreted as the interval mean. SN LK 11 p. 57 gives the finite impulse relation, and p. 58 prints the differential law with graphical interpretation. The mean-force task is a bounded preparation there. The five target views are the three BW views carrying this Klasse 10 place and the two SN views carrying the LK 11 place. A further 30 views reach it only as a prerequisite.
unsupportedClaims: BE/BB p. 21 describes force as temporal change of momentum in theme 3.1.4. Page 17 provides for selecting at least three of five themes in both course forms in year 11 at Berlin's integrated secondary schools and community schools and Brandenburg's comprehensive schools and vocational Gymnasien. This does not establish a mandatory RATE-M target in either Land.
HB and HH provide related impulse formulations. HE p. 30 prints vector F = ma. These pages and the diagnostic prerequisite placements do not extend the measured RATE-M target scope.

independentSourceFindings.reason: SN supplies the differential second law and interaction law, and BE/BB explicitly connect conservation with Newton's axioms, supporting a bounded proof operationalization. Full current projection support remains unresolved: BE/BB p.17 limits the introductory elective framework to specified school forms and selection of at least three of five themes, which does not establish a mandatory Gymnasium Q-phase target. HE p.30 does not explicitly demand this differential/integral proof formalism.
inspectedOfficialPages: official-pages/19-SN-official-extract.pdf: original physical pp.57–58; p.58 differential-law graphic inspected
official-pages/07-HE-official-extract.pdf: original physical pp.29–30; p.30 formula graphic inspected
unsupportedClaims: A mandatory Gymnasium Q-phase proof target in BE/BB cannot be established from the supplied school-form-conditional introductory elective pages.
The inspected broad clauses do not establish a nationwide mandatory obligation for this exact differential/integral proof.

independentSourceFindings.reason: SL p. 12 explicitly asks for a derivation from the interaction law for a central straight two-body collision. SN LK 11 pp. 57–58 supply conservation, the differential law, system/environment and action–reaction. These give a defensible basis for an advanced synthesis. The retained pages do not settle the official status of the complete proof with external impulses and both time conditions in all 32 native LK target views.
unsupportedClaims: HE lists the laws, momentum conservation and recoil. BE/BB conditionally connect conservation to Newton's axioms. Neither text explicitly mandates this general differential-and-integral proof in every projected course.

RP presents conservation as an axiom for balance reasoning. ST's elevated-level collision and recoil requirements support applications. These clauses do not verify the exact proof as a compulsory outcome.
An LK product placement, including one under changing electromagnetic fields in HH, cannot independently establish an official proof requirement or its teaching date.
